style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The fifth of the church's seven penitential psalms, and the one psalm whose title describes the person praying rather than naming an author: a prayer of an afflicted man, when he is faint. The first eleven verses are the strangest sick-report in the Psalter -- days going up in smoke, bones charred like a hearth, a heart struck and dried like grass, forgetting to eat, bones clinging to skin, a desert owl in the wilderness, a little owl among the ruins, a lone bird awake on a roof, ashes for bread and tears in the cup. And one line of theology about it: You lifted me up and threw me away. Then the pivot most laments turn on: But You, O LORD, sit enthroned forever. The dying man's timeline is suddenly not the one that matters. God will rise and have compassion on Zion because the appointed time has come; His servants love her very rubble; the nations will fear His name; a people not yet created will praise Him; the prisoner's groan is heard from heaven. Back in his own body -- strength broken on the road, days cut short -- he prays not to be taken in the middle of his life, and sets his half-life beside God's years. You laid the earth's foundation; the heavens are Your hands' work; they will wear out like a garment and You will change them like clothing, but You are the same, and Your years never end. Hebrews 1 quotes those three verses and addresses them to the Son. The psalm ends without the psalmist in it: the servants' children will live on, and their offspring be made firm before You, and that is enough.

1.text: A prayer of an afflicted man, when he is faint and pours out his complaint before the LORD. Hear my prayer, O LORD, and let my cry for help come through to You.
1.amp: A Prayer [tephillah] of ['for', ani, the KJV margin] the afflicted [ani], when he is overwhelmed [ataph -- faints], and pours out [shaphak] his complaint [siach] before [panim] the LORD [YHWH]. Hear [shama] my prayer [tephillah], O LORD [YHWH], and let my cry come [bo] unto You.
1.notes: tephillah le-ani khi-yaatoph (H8605, H6041, H5848): a prayer of an ani -- an afflicted man, unnamed: the one psalm whose title describes the person praying rather than naming an author -- when he FAINTS, ataph, Psalm 61:2's word. ve-li-phne YHWH yishpokh sicho (H6440, H3068, H8210, H7879): and pours out his siach, his complaint, before the LORD -- Hannah's verb (1 Samuel 1:15). YHWH shimah tephillati ve-shavati elekha tabo (H8085, H8605, H935): hear my prayer, and let my cry COME to You -- Psalm 88:2's request; the fifth of the church's seven penitential psalms opens like the darkest one.

2.text: Do not hide Your face from me in the day of my distress; bend Your ear to me; in the day I call, answer me quickly.
2.amp: Hide [satar] not Your face [panim] from me in the day [yom] when I am in trouble [tsar -- distress]; incline [natah] Your ear [ozen] unto me: in the day [yom] when I call [qara] answer [anah] me speedily [maher].
2.notes: al-taster panekha mimmenni be-yom tsar li (H5641, H6440, H3117, H6862): do not hide Your face in the day it is NARROW to me -- tsar, the hemmed-in word; hatteh-elai oznekha be-yom eqra maher aneni (H5186, H241, H7121, H4118, H6030): tilt Your ear, and in the day I call answer FAST. Three imperatives here, five counting verse 1's two, that most laments in the Psalter reach for; this one will earn them with the strangest illness-report in the book (vv. 3-11).

3.text: For my days go up in smoke, and my bones are charred like a hearth.
3.amp: For my days [yom] are consumed [kalah -- used up] like smoke ['into smoke', ashan, the KJV margin], and my bones [etsem] are burned [charar -- scorched] as an hearth.
3.notes: ki-khalu be-ashan yamai (H3615, H6227, H3117): for my days are finished 'in smoke' -- or, as the margin reads, INTO smoke: they do not end, they evaporate -- ve-atsmotai kemo-qed nicharu (H6106, H2787): and my bones are scorched -- the Hebrew divides it kemo-qed, 'like a burning'; read together as ke-moqed it is a hearth, a firebrand. Fever from the inside: Job 30:30's bones 'burned with heat', charar again, and the fire sent into the bones of Lamentations 1:13.

4.text: My heart has been struck down and dried up like grass, so that I even forget to eat my bread.
4.amp: My heart [leb] is smitten [nakah -- struck], and withered [yabesh] like grass [eseb]; so that I forget [shakach] to eat [akal] my bread [lechem].
4.notes: hukkah kha-eseb va-yibash libbi (H5221, H6212, H3001, H3820): my heart is STRUCK like grass and dried -- the morning-to-evening grass of Psalm 90:5-6, withered by the same verb -- ki-shakhachti me-akhol lachmi (H7911, H398, H3899): so that I have forgotten to eat my bread. The clinical sign of grief: the appetite goes first (cf. 1 Samuel 1:7).

5.text: From the sound of my own groaning, my bones have stuck fast to my skin.
5.amp: By reason of the voice [qol] of my groaning [anachah] my bones [etsem] cleave [dabaq -- cling] to my skin ['flesh', basar, the KJV margin].
5.notes: mi-qol anchati dabeqah atsmi li-besari (H6963, H585, H1692, H6106, H1320): from the voice of my groaning my bone CLINGS to my flesh -- the margin's word; wasting until the skeleton shows, Job 19:20's 'skin of my teeth'. The groaning is loud enough to be a cause.

6.text: I am like a desert owl of the wilderness; I have become like a little owl among the ruins.
6.amp: I am like [damah] a pelican of the wilderness [midbar]: I am like an owl [kos] of the desert [chorbah -- ruins].
6.notes: damiti li-qat midbar (H1819, H4057): I am like the qaat of the wilderness -- the KJV's pelican, more likely a desert owl or jackdaw, an unclean bird of the waste places (Leviticus 11:18; Isaiah 34:11). hayiti ke-khos chorabot (H3563, H2723): I have become like the kos of the ruins, the little owl -- spelled like the word for a cup, a different word. Two night-birds in empty country: the psalmist as a creature nobody wants near a house.

7.text: I lie awake; I have become like a lone bird on a rooftop.
7.amp: I watch, and am as a sparrow [tsippor] alone upon the house top [gag].
7.notes: shaqadti va-ehyeh ke-tsippor boded al-gag (H6833, H1406): I lie AWAKE -- shaqad, the watchman's verb, Jeremiah's almond-branch pun (Jeremiah 1:11-12) -- and I have become like a bird alone on a roof: the sparrow that has lost its mate, or the one the rest of the flock has left. Insomnia and isolation in one picture.

8.text: All day long my enemies taunt me; those who rave against me use my name as a curse.
8.amp: Mine enemies [oyeb] reproach [charaph -- taunt] me all the day [yom]; and they that are mad [halal -- rave] against me are sworn [shaba] against me.
8.notes: kol-ha-yom cherephuni oyebai (H3117, H2778, H341): all the day my enemies TAUNT me. meholalai bi nishbau (H1984, H7650): those raving against me -- halal in its mad sense, the word for David feigning insanity (1 Samuel 21:13) -- SWEAR by me: use my name as the standard curse, 'may you end up like him' (cf. Jeremiah 29:22). The sick man has become a proverb for ruin.

9.text: For I have eaten ashes as if they were bread, and mixed my drink with tears,
9.amp: For I have eaten [akal] ashes [epher] like bread [lechem], and mingled [masak] my drink with weeping [beki],
9.notes: ki-epher ka-lechem akhalti (H665, H3899, H398): for ashes like bread I have EATEN -- the mourner sits in ashes (Job 2:8) and here swallows them; ve-shiqquvai bi-bkhi masakhti (H1065, H4537): and my drinks with weeping I have MIXED -- masak, the verb for mixing wine, here tears for the spice. Psalm 42:3's bread of tears, with the ashes added.

10.text: because of Your indignation and Your fury -- for You lifted me up and threw me away.
10.amp: Because [panim] of Your indignation and Your wrath [qetseph]: for You have lifted me up [nasa], and cast me down [shalak -- flung me away].
10.notes: mi-pene-zaamekha ve-qitspekha (H6440, H7110): from the face of Your indignation and Your qetseph, Your breaking wrath -- ki nesatani va-tashlikheni (H5375, H7993): for You LIFTED me and THREW me -- the two verbs of a man picked up and hurled, Job 27:21's whirlwind. The psalm's one line of theology about the illness: it came from God's hand, and the penitent does not argue.

11.text: My days are like a shadow stretching out toward evening, and I am dried up like grass.
11.amp: My days [yom] are like a shadow [tsel] that declines [natah -- stretches out, lengthens]; and I am withered [yabesh] like grass [eseb].
11.notes: yamai ke-tsel natui (H3117, H6738, H5186): my days like a shadow STRETCHED OUT -- the late-afternoon shadow that lengthens just before it disappears, Psalm 109:23's -- va-ani ka-eseb ibash (H6212, H3001): and I, like grass, dry up -- verse 4's image closing the complaint. Eleven verses of a man dying; then verse 12, and the word 'But'.

12.text: But You, O LORD, sit enthroned forever, and Your remembrance lasts from generation to generation.
12.amp: But You, O LORD [YHWH], shall endure [yashab -- sit enthroned, remain] for ever [olam]; and Your remembrance [zeker -- memorial, Name] unto all generations [dor -- generation].
12.notes: ve-attah YHWH le-olam tesheb (H3068, H5769, H3427): BUT YOU, LORD -- the pivot of the whole psalm, the pronoun that turns nearly every lament in the Psalter, Psalm 88 being the terrible exception -- forever You SIT, enthroned, Psalm 9:7's and 29:10's verb; ve-zikhrekha le-dor va-dor (H2143, H1755): and Your zeker, Your memorial Name (Exodus 3:15), to 'generation and generation'. The man whose days are smoke sets them beside the One whose years do not move; verses 25-27 will finish the comparison.

13.text: You Yourself will rise up and show compassion on Zion, for it is time to be gracious to her -- yes, the appointed time has come.
13.amp: You shall arise [qum], and have mercy [racham -- show compassion] upon Zion [Tsiyyon]: for the time [et] to favour [chanan -- be gracious to] her, yea, the set time [moed -- appointed time], is come [bo].
13.notes: attah taqum terachem Tsiyyon (H6965, H7355, H6726): YOU will rise and have COMPASSION on Zion -- racham, the womb-word; ki-et le-chenenah ki-ba moed (H6256, H2603, H935, H4150): for it is time to be gracious to her -- the MOED, the appointed hour, has come: Jeremiah's seventy years running out (Jeremiah 29:10; Daniel 9:2). The individual's illness widens to the city's ruin, and the psalmist's own timeline is suddenly not the one that matters.

14.text: For Your servants take pleasure in her very stones and are gracious even toward her dust.
14.amp: For Your servants [ebed] take pleasure [ratsah -- delight] in her stones [eben], and favour [chanan -- feel pity for] the dust [afar] thereof.
14.notes: ki-ratsu abadekha et-abaneha (H7521, H5650, H68): for Your servants DELIGHT in her stones -- the rubble; ve-et-apharah yechonenu (H6083, H2603): and her dust they feel tender toward -- chanan, the grace-verb, aimed at debris. Nehemiah weeping over the report of the walls (Nehemiah 1:3-4) is this verse; love for a place is measured by what you feel about its ruins.

15.text: Then will the nations stand in awe of the LORD's name, and every king of the earth of Your glory,
15.amp: So the heathen [goy -- nations] shall fear [yare] the name [shem] of the LORD [YHWH], and all the kings [melek] of the earth [eretz] Your glory [kabod].
15.notes: ve-yireu goyim et-shem YHWH (H3372, H1471, H8034, H3068): and the nations will FEAR the name of the LORD -- ve-khol-malkhe ha-arets et-kebodekha (H4428, H776, H3519): and all the kings of the earth Your glory. Zion rebuilt as a missionary event: Isaiah 60:3's kings coming to the brightness of her rising.

16.text: for the LORD will have built Zion; He will have appeared in His glory;
16.amp: When the LORD [YHWH] shall build up [banah] Zion [Tsiyyon], He shall appear [raah -- be seen] in His glory [kabod].
16.notes: ki-banah YHWH Tsiyyon (H1129, H3068, H6726): for the LORD has BUILT Zion -- the Hebrew perfect, the future so sure it is spoken as done -- nirah bi-khbodo (H7200, H3519): He has been SEEN in His glory. The rebuilt city as a theophany: God is visible in a restored people the way He was in the pillar of fire.

17.text: He will have turned toward the prayer of the destitute, and He will not have despised their prayer.
17.amp: He will regard [panah -- turn to face] the prayer [tephillah] of the destitute, and not despise [bazah] their prayer [tephillah].
17.notes: panah el-tephillat ha-arar (H6437, H8605): He has TURNED to the prayer of the arar -- the stripped, the destitute: a rare word, the desert shrub of Jeremiah 17:6 -- ve-lo-bazah et-tephillatam (H959, H8605): and has not DESPISED their prayer. The prayer of verse 1, answered in advance in the third person; the afflicted man has found himself inside a larger petition.

18.text: Let this be written down for the generation to come, so that a people yet to be created may praise Yah:
18.amp: This shall be written [kathab] for the generation [dor] to come [acharon -- the later one]: and the people [am] which shall be created [bara] shall praise [halal] the LORD [Yah].
18.notes: tikkateb zot le-dor acharon (H3789, H1755, H314): let this be WRITTEN for the generation after -- the psalm knows it is a document; ve-am nibra yehallel-Yah (H5971, H1254, H1984, H3050): and a people CREATED -- bara, Genesis 1:1's verb, a people God makes from nothing -- will praise Yah. Psalm 22:31's 'a people that shall be born', and 1 Peter 2:10's people who were not a people: the church reads its own birth certificate here.

19.text: For He looked down from His holy height; from heaven the LORD gazed at the earth,
19.amp: For He has looked down [shaqaph -- leaned over to look] from the height [marom] of His sanctuary [qodesh]; from heaven [shamayim] did the LORD [YHWH] behold [nabat -- gaze at] the earth [eretz];
19.notes: ki-hishqiph mi-merom qodsho (H8259, H4791, H6944): for He LEANED DOWN from the height of His holiness -- shaqaph, Psalm 14:2's window-verb -- YHWH mi-shamayim el-erets hibbit (H3068, H8064, H776, H5027): the LORD from heaven at the earth GAZED. The same look that found no one seeking God in Psalm 14 here finds a prisoner groaning.

20.text: to hear the groaning of the prisoner, to set free those doomed to death,
20.amp: To hear [shama] the groaning [anaqah] of the prisoner [asir]; to loose [pathach -- open] those that are appointed ['the children of death', ben, the KJV margin] to death;
20.notes: lishmoa enqat asir (H8085, H603, H615): to HEAR the groaning of the prisoner -- Psalm 79:11's asir, the exile in his cell -- le-phatteach bene temutah (H6605, H1121): to OPEN 'the sons of death', the margin's literal -- the condemned. Isaiah 61:1's opening of the prison, which Jesus read as His own job description (Luke 4:18).

21.text: so that the name of the LORD may be recounted in Zion, and His praise in Jerusalem,
21.amp: To declare [saphar -- recount] the name [shem] of the LORD [YHWH] in Zion [Tsiyyon], and His praise [tehillah] in Jerusalem;
21.notes: le-sapper be-Tsiyyon shem YHWH (H5608, H6726, H8034, H3068): to RECOUNT in Zion the name of the LORD -- u-tehillato bi-Yrushalaim (H8416): and His praise in Jerusalem. The purpose clause of the whole rescue: freed prisoners are for telling. Psalm 9:14's 'that I may tell out all Your praise in the gates', for a nation.

22.text: when peoples are gathered into one, and kingdoms with them, to serve the LORD.
22.amp: When the people [am -- peoples] are gathered [qabats] together [yachad], and the kingdoms [mamlakah], to serve [abad -- worship] the LORD [YHWH].
22.notes: be-hiqqabets ammim yachdav (H6908, H5971, H3162): when the peoples are GATHERED together -- u-mamlakhot la-abod et-YHWH (H4467, H5647, H3068): and the kingdoms, to SERVE the LORD -- abad, the worship-word. The vision of Psalm 87 and Isaiah 2:2-3: a Jerusalem that the nations come up to, not a Jerusalem in rubble. The psalm has traveled from one sick man's bed to the end of history in ten verses.

23.text: He has worn my strength down on the road; He has cut my days short.
23.amp: He weakened ['afflicted', anah, the KJV margin] my strength [koach] in the way [derek -- on the road]; He shortened [qatsar] my days [yom].
23.notes: innah ba-derekh kochi (H6031, H1870, H3581): He AFFLICTED -- the margin's verb -- my strength on the road: the pilgrim who will not reach the city; qitsar yamai (H7114, H3117): He CUT SHORT my days -- qatsar, spelled like the reaping verb though it is the other root: to be cut short. After the vision, the psalmist is back in his own body, and the contrast is the point of verses 24-27.

24.text: I said, 'My God, do not take me away in the middle of my days -- You, whose years run through all generations!'
24.amp: I said [amar], O my God [El], take me not away [alah -- do not bring me up] in the midst of my days [yom]: Your years [shanah] are throughout all generations [dor -- generation].
24.notes: omar Eli al-taaleni ba-chatsi yamai (H559, H410, H5927, H3117): I say, my God, do not TAKE me UP -- alah, the verb used when flame and smoke go up off a ruined city, an ironic answer to the smoke his days went up in back in verse 3, where the word was kalah, spent -- in the half of my days: the prayer of every man who dies young, Hezekiah's (Isaiah 38:10); be-dor dorim shenotekha (H1755, H8141): 'in generation of generations are Your years'. The man with half a life left addresses the One with no ends at all -- and the next three verses are the Psalter's fullest statement of it, the one the writer of Hebrews reached for when he needed words for the Son.

25.text: You founded the earth long ago, and the heavens are the work of Your own hands.
25.amp: Of old [panim -- before] have You laid the foundation [yasad] of the earth [eretz]: and the heavens [shamayim] are the work [maaseh] of Your hands [yad].
25.notes: le-phanim ha-arets yasadta (H6440, H776, H3245): 'to the face' -- beforehand, long ago -- the earth You FOUNDED; u-maaseh yadekha shamayim (H4639, H3027, H8064): and the work of Your hands, the heavens -- Psalm 8:3's fingers, Psalm 104:5's foundations. Hebrews 1:10-12 quotes verses 25-27 whole and addresses them to the Son: 'Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth' -- the psalm's Creator is, the apostle says, Christ.

26.text: They will perish, but You will stand; all of them will wear out like a garment; like clothing You will change them, and they will be changed.
26.amp: They shall perish [abad], but You shall endure ['stand', amad, the KJV margin]: yea, all of them shall wax old [balah -- wear out] like a garment [beged]; as a vesture [lebush -- clothing] shall You change [chalaph] them, and they shall be changed [chalaph]:
26.notes: hemmah yobedu ve-attah taamod (H6, H5975): THEY will perish -- the heavens and the earth -- and You will STAND, the margin's literal. ve-khullam ka-beged yiblu (H899, H1086): all of them like a garment wear out -- Isaiah 51:6's heavens vanishing like smoke. ka-lebush tachaliphem ve-yachalophu (H3830, H2498): like clothing You will CHANGE them, and they will be changed. Creation as God's wardrobe: worn, folded, replaced -- and the Wearer the same forever (cf. 2 Peter 3:10-13; Revelation 21:1).

27.text: But You are the same, and Your years will never come to an end.
27.amp: But You are the same, and Your years [shanah] shall have no end [tamam -- be finished].
27.notes: ve-attah-hu: 'and You -- He' -- the Hebrew's shortest way of saying 'You are the same one': the ani hu of Isaiah 41:4 and 48:12, the divine self-identification John's Gospel hears in 'I am He' (John 8:24, 58). u-shenotekha lo yittammu (H8141, H8552): and Your years are not FINISHED -- tamam, the verb for a supply spent to the last of it (Genesis 47:18's money, Deuteronomy 2:16's generation). Hebrews 1:12 quotes it of the Son, and Hebrews 13:8 echoes it: the same yesterday, today, and forever.

28.text: The children of Your servants will live on, and their offspring will be made firm before You.
28.amp: The children [ben] of Your servants [ebed] shall continue [shakan -- settle, dwell], and their seed [zera] shall be established [kun] before [panim] You.
28.notes: bene-abadekha yishkonu (H1121, H5650, H7931): the sons of Your servants will DWELL -- shakan, the tabernacle-verb, settled and staying -- ve-zaram le-phanekha yikkon (H2233, H6440, H3559): and their seed before Your face will be made FIRM. The afflicted man who asked not to die in the middle of his days ends by not mentioning himself: the unchanging God guarantees a future to the servants' children, and that is enough. The fifth penitential psalm closes on the next generation.
